where: Section 1 (also Exam trap 2 and Quiz Q2)
problem: The chapter says growing depends on the order of visiting neighbours and that 'two runs with different orders can give slightly different borders'. With the predicate actually defined, P(x,y): |f(x,y) − f(x_s,y_s)| ≤ T, this is false. P depends only on the pixel's own value and the fixed seed value, so every pixel connected to the seed by a path of pixels satisfying P is accepted, in any order. The grown set is exactly the connected component of the seed in {pixels with value in [f(seed)−T, f(seed)+T]}. A rejected pixel can never become acceptable later, so queue order cannot open or block a path. Order matters only when P uses running region statistics (for example the mean of the region grown so far) or a neighbour-difference rule such as |f(x,y) − f(accepted neighbour)| ≤ T. Quiz Q2's answer is therefore wrong as stated.
fix: Replace with: 'With P fixed on the seed value, the accepted set is the connected component of the seed, so visit order does not change it. Order can change the result only when P uses statistics of the region grown so far, such as its running mean, or compares a pixel with its accepted neighbour instead of the seed.' Rewrite trap 2 as: 'Say clearly whether P is fixed on the seed value (order does not matter) or on the current region mean/neighbour (order can matter); state which one the question uses.' Rewrite Q2: 'Two runs give different borders only because P is defined on the evolving region, e.g. |f(x,y) − mean of region so far| ≤ T; the mean changes as pixels are added, so the order of adding changes which pixels pass.'

problem: It says 'the final regions are the leaves of the quadtree after allowed merges'. After merging, a region can join leaves that sit under different parents, so the merged region is a union of quadtree leaves, not a leaf, and its boundary does not follow quadtree lines. Q7's 'leaves are the regions left after splitting and allowed merges' has the same slip.
fix: Say: 'Splitting gives quadtree leaves. Merging combines adjacent leaves, possibly from different parents, so each final region is a union of quadtree leaves, not itself a node of the tree.' In Q7: 'The tree stores the splitting stage: each internal node is a region that was split into four children, and the leaves are the unsplit blocks. Merging then joins adjacent leaves, so final regions are unions of leaves.'

problem: 'Region growing is the base of superpixel methods such as SLIC' is inaccurate. SLIC forms superpixels by clustering pixels on colour plus (x,y) position, in the spirit of k-means, not by seeded region growing. Seeded region growing underlies other superpixel and interactive segmentation methods.
fix: Say: 'Seeded region growing is the base of several superpixel and interactive segmentation methods; SLIC, for example, instead clusters pixels on colour and position, k-means style, to get small uniform patches before classification.'
